data.value: TR + the province's plate code (2 digits) + 10 digits, e.g. TR520401200241. The plate code is compared with your directorate's province.

data.name: Reg78.Info.Mismatch
data.value: If the number starts with another province's plate code (for example, a migratory beekeeper registered in Ordu who keeps an apiary here), write a short reason. It is kept with the registration.

data.name: Reg78.Info.PublicName
data.value: Without this consent, public pages such as the Honey Story show a fixed code like BK-7F3K9Q2M instead of the name. It is the same code everywhere, so the honey stays traceable to one beekeeper without naming them.

data.name: Reg78.Info.Education
data.value: Not needed for traceability; leave it empty unless the beekeeper wants it recorded.

data.name: Reg78.Info.Purpose
data.value: The beekeeper's main product, such as honey. Choose one; it does not limit what the beekeeper can deliver.

data.name: Reg78.Info.NoPhone
data.value: Without a mobile phone the beekeeper cannot confirm with an SMS code. Print the form, let the beekeeper sign it and upload a photo; the registration then waits for your Compliance Officer.

data.name: Reg78.Info.Language
data.value: The beekeeper receives the SMS code and later messages in this language.

data.name: Cust.Info.Number
data.value: Type the beekeeper's holding identification number (e.g. TR520401200241) or platform number and press Find. The beekeeper's apiaries then appear in the form.

data.name: Ci.Info.Arrival
data.value: Normally the container arrives unsealed: take the samples, then close it with one seal. Choose “sealed at harvest” only when the association's field inspector sealed it at the apiary with a seal from the association's pool; check that the seal is intact.

data.name: Ci.Info.Jars
data.value: Fill two jars from this container. Put a seal label from the pool over cap and jar on each: the sample jar goes to the laboratory, the counter-sample jar stays with you in case a result is disputed.

data.name: Ci.Info.Reseal
data.value: Taking the samples opens the container. Seal it again and type the new seal number; the container keeps this seal until it is used.

data.name: Ci.Info.CounterLocation
data.value: Where the counter-sample jars are stored, e.g. “Cold room 2, shelf B”. Keep them until the date next to it, in case a result is disputed.

data.name: Ci.Cap.SafetyButton.Help
data.value: Vacuum cap, as on baby-food jars: the button stays down only while there is a vacuum.

data.name: Ci.Cap.TamperRing.Help

data.name: Ci.InfoCard.Button.Title
data.value: Safety-button cap: how to close the jar

data.name: Ci.InfoCard.Button
data.value: The button stays down only with a vacuum in the jar. After filling, draw the vacuum with a hand vacuum pump until the button goes down. Never heat the honey to get a vacuum: heat raises HMF and lowers diastase, so the sample would no longer show the honey as delivered.

data.name: Ci.InfoCard.Ring.Title
data.value: Tamper-ring cap: how to close the jar

data.name: Ci.InfoCard.Ring
data.value: Turn the cap until the ring sits tight under it. An unbroken ring shows the jar has not been opened; a broken ring means it was.

data.name: Ci.InfoCard.Closure
data.value: Beekeepers bring their own tins and buckets, and most arrive unsealed. Take the samples first, then close the container with one seal in front of the beekeeper. Choose per container:

data.name: Ci.InfoCard.Closure.Pool
data.value: Seal labels and plastic seals come from your organization's seal pool; each code is used once.

data.name: Ci.Closure.SealLabel.Short
data.value: Numbered label with QR across lid and body. Works on any container.

data.name: Ci.Closure.SealLabel.Help
data.value: A numbered label with a QR code, issued by the platform and printed in advance on tamper-evident VOID label stock. It goes across lid and body and tears or leaves VOID marks if someone removes it. Works on any container.

data.name: Ci.Closure.PlasticSeal.Short
data.value: Through a handle or a lid hole; it locks once.

data.name: Ci.Closure.PlasticSeal.Help
data.value: For containers with a handle or a lid hole: the purchased numbered seal goes through it and locks; it can only be opened by cutting it.

data.name: Ci.Closure.OrgContainer.Short
data.value: Registered once; scan or type its TK code.

data.name: Ci.Closure.OrgContainer.Help
data.value: The association's own container, registered once with a permanent code and QR. Scan or type its code at the delivery; its page shows every use. It is still closed with a seal from the pool.

data.name: Ci.Info.Closure
data.value: The container is closed once, after sampling, in front of the beekeeper. The seal comes from your organization's seal pool.

data.name: Ci.Info.CapCheck
data.value: Check both jars after closing them. A raised button or a broken ring means the jar was opened: discard it and fill a new one.

data.name: Ci.ClosingHelp
data.value: After sampling, close the container in front of the beekeeper and scan or type the seal.

data.name: Ci.SealDup
data.value: This code is already used in this delivery.

data.name: Ci.Confirms
data.value: The SMS code confirms exactly this list: every container code, every seal code and the jar cap. If anything changes later, the record no longer matches the confirmation.

data.name: Lab.Info.Reception
data.value: Answer three checks: the seal label code matches the record, the label is intact (no tear, no VOID marks), and the cap is closed (button down or ring unbroken). Any “no” rejects the jar, because it may have been opened on the way. The plant then takes a new jar from the same container, which is still closed with its seal; the counter-sample stays with the plant for a dispute.

data.name: Scene.label
data.value: A seal label goes across lid and body. Peeled off, it tears and leaves VOID marks.

data.name: Scene.plastic
data.value: A numbered plastic seal goes through the handle and locks.

data.name: Scene.scan
data.value: The association's container is scanned by its QR code.

data.name: Scene.button
data.value: Button down: the jar is closed. A raised button: the jar was opened.

data.name: Scene.ring
data.value: Ring unbroken: the jar is closed. A broken ring: the jar was opened.

data.name: Seal.Help
data.value: Every seal used at a delivery comes from this pool: seal labels issued by the platform and purchased numbered plastic seals. Each code is used once; here you see which codes are free, where each one was used and which were opened.

data.name: Seal.Materials
data.value: Tamper-evident VOID label stock (100 × 50 mm) for the seal labels, numbered plastic seals for handles, sample jars with safety-button or tamper-ring caps, and a hand vacuum pump for the button caps.

data.name: Seal.RangeHelp
